label: Optimal RTU — Delaney et al. 2005 (as published in RadMaps preprint, uncorrected)
source: Delaney G, Jacob S, Featherstone C, Barton M. The role of radiotherapy in cancer treatment: estimating optimal utilization from a review of evidence-based clinical guidelines. Cancer 2005;104(6):1129-37
intent_coverage: First-course external-beam indications from clinical guidelines, curative AND palliative; overall 52.3%. Palliative first courses ≈ 14% of all new patients (Jacob et al. 2010, Clin Oncol 22:56-64).
mapping_notes: Values exactly as used for the arXiv 2605.23456 results; retained frozen for reproducibility. Against the world case mix this set implies an effective RTU of 58.7% rather than Delaney's 52.3% because several entries do not match the source (Jacob et al. 2010 Table 1 tabulates the Delaney-era per-site rates): Thyroid 1.00 (source 0.10), Colorectum 0.50 (source colon 0.14 / rectum 0.65 ≈ 0.31 weighted), head-and-neck subsites 0.10–1.00 (source single figure 0.78). The 0.35 used for the gynaecological sites is Delaney's own single gynecologic rate, so those entries are faithful to Delaney 2005 Table 1 (Jacob et al. 2010 later split them). Use delaney_2005_corrected for the faithful 2005 model.

label: Optimal RTU — Delaney et al. 2005 (Table 1, as published)
source: Delaney G, Jacob S, Featherstone C, Barton M. The role of radiotherapy in cancer treatment: estimating optimal utilization from a review of evidence-based clinical guidelines. Cancer 2005;104(6):1129-37, Table 1 (overall 52.3%).
intent_coverage: First-course external-beam indications, curative AND palliative; overall 52.3%. Palliative first courses ≈ 14% of all new patients (Jacob et al. 2010).
mapping_notes: GLOBOCAN type ← Delaney site: Colorectum = colon 14% & rectum 61% weighted by Delaney's proportions 0.09:0.05 → 0.308; Cervix uteri, Corpus uteri, Ovary, Vagina, Vulva ← Gynecologic 35% (Delaney gives a single rate); Kidney ← Renal 27%; Lip/oral, Oropharynx, Hypopharynx, Nasopharynx, Larynx, Salivary glands ← Head and neck 78%; NHL & Hodgkin ← Lymphoma 65%; Multiple myeloma ← Myeloma 38%; Kaposi sarcoma, Mesothelioma, Penis, Other cancers ← Other 50%; NMSC → 0. Jacob et al. 2010 (Clin Oncol 22:56-64, Table 1) re-analysed this model and differs only for rectum (65), kidney (28) and the split gynaecological sites.

label: Optimal RTU — CCORE 2012 model (Barton et al. 2014; per-site values from Wong et al. 2016 Table 1)
source: Barton MB, Jacob S, Shafiq J, Wong K, Thompson SR, Hanna TP, Delaney GP. Estimating the demand for radiotherapy from the evidence: a review of changes from 2003 to 2012. Radiother Oncol 2014;112(1):140-4. Per-site values transcribed from Wong K, Delaney GP, Barton MB. Radiother Oncol 2016;119(1):145-9, Table 1.
intent_coverage: Updated 2012 CCORE model; overall 48.4% (Wong 2016 Table 1; 48.3% in Barton 2014). First-course indications, curative AND palliative: 77% of first courses radical (24.3 fractions) and 23% palliative (3.0 fractions), mean 19.4 fractions per course.
mapping_notes: GLOBOCAN type ← Wong site: Colorectum = colon 4% & rectum 60% weighted by Australian incidence 8.4:4.2 → 0.227; Lip/oral, Oropharynx, Hypopharynx, Nasopharynx, Larynx, Salivary glands ← Head and neck 74%; NHL & Hodgkin ← Lymphoma 73%; Corpus uteri ← Uterus 32%; Multiple myeloma ← Myeloma 45%; Kaposi sarcoma, Mesothelioma, Penis, Other cancers ← Other 19%; NMSC not in model → 0.
